title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 113
paragraphs: Then Masistes, not yet having heard any of these things but supposing that some evil had fallen on him, came running to his house; and seeing his wife thus mutilated, at once he took counsel with his sons and set out to go to Bactria together with them — and doubtless some others as well — intending to make the province of Bactria revolt and to do the greatest possible injury to the king. This in fact would have come to pass, I believe, if he had reached the land of the Bactrians and Sacans before he was overtaken, for they were much attached to him and he was moreover governor of the Bactrians. But Xerxes, informed that he was doing this, sent an army after him on his way and killed him, his sons, and his army. So much for what happened about Xerxes's passion and the death of Masistes.
